page.overview:
Who is Geoff Crossley?

Geoff Crossley (born 11 May 1921 and died 7 January 2002) was British racing driver who participated in two Formula One Grand Prix in using a privateer .

Following World War II, Crossley began his racing career by entering an Alta in the 1947 British Empire Trophy. In 1949, he ordered an Alta GP from the manufacturer and began racing in various non-championship events.

He made his Formula One championship debut at the 1950 British Grand Prix, but his race ended prematurely due to a transmission failure. A month later he entered his second and final Formula One race at the 1950 Belgian Grand Prix, finishing in 9th position.

He retired from racing at the end of the 1950 season, citing the high costs of racing. He made a brief motorsport return after building a special is called the Berkshire Special. He entered the 1955 Richmond Trophy race at Goodwood Circuit, but the car was slowest in practice and he decided to withdraw from the event.
